Mistweaver Monk Rotation in 

Mistweaver Monk's priority and rotation relies entirely on juggling short-duration cooldowns, buffs and procs, and managing mana consumption to be maximized with damage dealt on your group. 

 Align Procs With Damage: Hold healing procs (like Zen Pulse, Spiritfont, Strength of the Black Ox) for heavier incoming damage rather than spending them freely during downtime.
 

 Keep Mana at the Forefront: Mana management is a constant priority throughout any encounter. Downtime is your best opportunity to spend Mana Tea stacks, ensuring you enter the next damage window with the headroom to sustain your output.
 

 Managing Haste: Haste is one of the more intense aspects of Mistweaver's gameplay. When active, it accelerates your abilities and brings cooldowns back faster, creating high-intensity windows that demand quick decision-making to get the most out of.

 Pre-Combat Check

 Before any combat happens, it is important for Mistweaver Monk to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.

 Mistweaver Monk Responding to Incoming Damage

 Single Target

 Single target healing is one of Mistweaver's core strengths. Our toolkit allows for quick, flexible responses to incoming damage, with options that scale based on how much time you have to react. In this context, "single target" refers to healing one individual - whether that's a tank, a party member, or yourself.

 Light Single Target Damage

 Light damage consists of small, non-threatening hits that don't demand immediate attention which is handled naturally by your HoTs - primarily Renewing Mist that scales with your lowest-hp ally via Mistline. Since you should already be maintaining HoTs on the group, minimal additional action is needed when someone takes light damage.

 With Jadefire Teachings talented, leveraging the damage-to-heal conversion to continue attacking while healing the injured ally is a smart move. Ancient Teachings intelligently splits its total healing evenly between (up to 5) injured allies, meaning a single injured player receives the full heal. This allows you to maintain damage output in a mana-efficient way without wasting procs that could be saved for heavier damage phases.

 Medium Single Target Damage

 Medium damage typically involves a single hit that drops an ally to roughly 50% health. Your response depends on whether additional damage is incoming.

 If follow-up damage is expected, Life Cocoon is your safest option, but might be more beneficial for heavy damage. The absorb buys you breathing room for continuous healing on your target. Use this at your own discretion.

 If no follow-up damage is expected, assess your available procs. A Strength of the Black Ox proc, for instance, can quickly apply a powerful Enveloping Mist HoT while providing group-wide shields effectively handling the situation without further input. Similarly, Spiritfont is an even stronger version of the previous, as its healing is redirected from split-between-five to fully on the single injured target alongside applying Chi Cocoons on your group, though this could be instead saved for AoE damage.

 For both Raid and Mythic+ content, Vivify/Sheilun's Gift serve as your primary quick-response tools. When paired with Vivacious Vivification, these become instant-cast, enabling rapid reactions to further damage on the target. However, they come with trade-offs: high mana costs, consumption of procs better suited for AoE healing (like Zen Pulse), and in Sheilun's Gift's case, the use of stacked clouds that could deliver stronger AoE healing.

 As with light damage, Jadefire Teachings talented allows you to maintain pressing Rising Sun Kick on cooldown in order to keep consistent maintenance healing rolling.

 Heavy Single Target Damage

 Heavy damage scenarios include sustained high-damage DoTs, tanks taking sustained damage without defensive cooldowns, or party members who've pulled aggro. Since we already discussed using Life Cocoon in medium damage situations, heavy damage is the natural point to fully commit to the external.

 This is where you'll reach for Mistweaver's strongest single-target healing tool: Soothing Mist. Beyond making your Vivify, Sheilun's Gift, and Enveloping Mist instant cast during the channel, it also provides passive healing through its own HoT effect and additional damage reduction from Elusive Mists at the cost of one extra (though shortened) global cooldown. It's worth noting that this sequence is only necessary when you need to cast several Vivify or Sheilun's Gifts back-to-back on a single target in genuine danger, not as a default response. If the previous damage tiers (light and medium) are still holding things together, there's no need to escalate here.

 AoE

 AoE healing is where Mistweaver truly shines. With the right setup, you can keep your entire party alive through heavy damage phases. The key is being proactive rather than reactive, entering damage events already ramped and ready to perform, though there will be moments where you need quick reactions to incoming damage.

 Light AoE Damage

 Light AoE damage consists of small hits across multiple allies that don't require immediate attention. This is where your HoTs, especially Renewing Mist, do most of the heavy lifting. Keeping them up on your group allows for passive healing that handles light AoE without needing to actively spend globals.

 With Jadefire Teachings talented, you can continue dealing damage while healing multiple injured allies with Ancient Teachings. It splits its total healing evenly among up to 5 injured targets, making it an efficient way to handle light AoE without burning procs better saved for heavier phases.

 Medium AoE Damage

 This is where you need to actively respond to incoming damage. As a general rule, begin thinking about cooldown usage here. Mistweaver has several at its disposal: Revival, Invoke Yu'lon, the Jade Serpent/Invoke Chi-Ji, the Red Crane, Celestial Conduit, and Thunder Focus Tea (the latter functioning as a minor cooldown given its attached effects). Ideally, you've already ramped ahead of the damage, so your HoTs and amplifying effects are in place to maximize their value. See the ramping and major cooldowns sections for more detail.

 Procs in medium damage are no longer held; they're spent to handle outgoing damage, so use them wisely:
 Strength of the Black Ox procs should be directed at targets actively taking damage to maximize Enveloping Mist's HoT and the group-wide shields.
Spiritfont procs are equally valuable here, providing strong split healing that naturally favors injured targets over time, along with Chi Cocoons on your group.

 The second and third points of Spiritfont amplify abilities you're already casting: Rising Sun Kick (particularly with Jadefire Teachings for consistent maintenance healing) and Enveloping Mist's HoT, respectively.

 With Zen Pulse, these casts are the perfect time to let those stacks you've been holding onto rip onto the Raid, capitalizing on the Renewing Mists you've been generating the entire fight.

 A few Vivify/Sheilun's Gift casts can quickly spot-heal those in the most danger, especially when paired with Vivacious Vivification for instant casts. Just be mindful of the mana cost, and consider whether those procs are better saved for a heavier damage phase ahead. Keep in mind, taking a big Mana Tea chug to gain stacks via Tranquil Tea grants Sheilun's Gift a stronger AoE heal as opposed to mostly being single-target focused.

 Heavy AoE Damage

 Heavy damage is where cooldowns stop being optional and become a requirement. Everything from the medium damage phase still applies, but cooldown usage is now guaranteed, and back-to-back cooldowns are sometimes necessary to keep up with the incoming damage.

 This section isn't quite too long, but the key point is that for heavy damage, it is almost always sustained long enough that you are holding onto the points made in medium damage for prolonged periods of time, often utilizing cooldowns back-to-back to keep up with the damage. For instance, you might find yourself pressing Revival during a large dip of damage while Invoke Chi-Ji, the Red Crane is active, and then following up the cooldown with large stacked Sheilun's Gift at the end to top off the damage.

 During heavy damage, make sure to strategically and continuously hop between players using Vivify/Sheilun's Gift to ensure you're healing the most injured targets, not allowing them to die. Life Cocoon is a phenomenal external that we can make use of in these moments, as we can practically ignore a player during the heavy damage. 

 Ramping

 Almost all healers have some form of a ramp: a way to build up healing ahead of incoming damage. Mistweaver is no exception, using short-duration HoTs to create powerful burst windows that can be timed directly around incoming damage spikes.

 Mythic+

 In Mythic+, the number of Enveloping Mist casts required within a ramp scales directly with the incoming damage. As key levels increase, more casts are needed, and the time spent ramping grows accordingly.

 Ramping is not a strict requirement to perform well, but it is a powerful tool that pays off significantly when mastered. The general process is as follows:

 For lighter incoming damage, fewer Enveloping Mist casts are sufficient, and prioritizing your squishiest party members is generally the right call.

 Soothing Mist in general is covered further in the Advanced Soothing Mist section, but it is worth noting here that the time savings from Soothing Mist only kick in after the second Enveloping Mist cast. Avoid using it as a ramp tool unless you're committing to 3 or more casts in a row.

 Raid

 Ramping in Raid is less flexible than Mythic+, as our gameplay is largely built around cooldown windows with maintenance healing in between. Ramps revolve around strategic Heart of the Jade Serpent windows, which return faster cooldown rates and allow us to place and immediately extend several Renewing Mists across the group, followed by cooldowns or direct Zen Pulse stack spending to cleave healing onto the raid.

 A second form of ramping involves using Invoke Yu'lon, the Jade Serpent earlier than damage hits to line up Vivify with high incoming damage. See the major cooldowns section for more detail on the Yu'lon ramp specifically.

 Mistweaver Monk Major Cooldowns

Mistweaver Monks have a wide variety of cooldowns available to use that offer differing profiles of healing requirements, though some can and do get molded to match whatever might be necessary to counter! Knowing how you can utilize these cooldowns over others allows for quicker understanding and mastering of the specialization without question.

Thunder Focus Tea

Thunder Focus Tea's synergy with Mistweaver's kit is extensive and is thought to be one of Mistweaver's most overloaded buttons due to these interactions. Though not specifically seen in the same caliber of a cooldown as something plannable like Revival, it can be considered a "rotational" cooldown and one that can (& should!) be paired with other cooldowns to give more... oomph!

At a baseline, the spell is incredibly simple in its functions: it empowers the next spell cast to grant that spell additional functionality:
Enveloping Mist - Instantly place an Enveloping Mist on your target, ignoring the original cast time, while also healing them instantly for the total HoT amount.
Renewing Mist - Increase the duration of the resulting Renewing Mist by +10 seconds.
Rising Sun Kick - Reduce the incoming cooldown of Rising Sun Kick by 9 seconds.

However, there are several talents that we can choose from that strengthen Thunder Focus Tea further: 
Spiritfont - Guarantees a Spiritfont stack as soon as you press Thunder Focus Tea.
Deep Clarity - Guarantees a Zen Pulse stack on consumption of the empower.
Focused Thunder - Grants an additional usage of an empower per Thunder Focus Tea cast.
Secret Infusion - Grants a semi-permanent buff that increases a Secondary Stat relative to the chosen empowered ability.

Enveloping Mist - Grants Secret Infusion (Critical Strike).
Renewing Mist - Grants Secret Infusion (Haste).
Rising Sun Kick - Grants Secret Infusion (Versatility).

Morning Breeze - Instantly resets the remaining cooldown on Rising Sun Kick.
Jade Infusion - Places a Jade Serpent Statue at your feet.

Along those lines, there are many "combos" we can choose to do with Thunder Focus Tea to make gameplay a bit more interesting with weaving in different abilities that might not be the most clear at first glance. Take a look at the Advanced Thunder Focus Tea section for more details.

Though both Hero Trees add additional benefits to Thunder Focus Tea, there are distinct differences in their use cases.

Specifically with , our aim is to use Thunder Focus Tea as often as possible, given that its own cast offers quickened cooldown rates to itself (and other spells!) via Heart of the Jade Serpent. Sitting on the cooldown is effectively a healing loss the longer it sits off cooldown, especially if Heart of the Jade Serpent is active when it should be actively cooling down during this window. 

On the other hand, 's Endless Draught's two charges give us flexibility on its usage, meaning that holding onto one charge of the cooldown to pair with damage events and/or other cooldowns (without overcapping both charges) is integral to the success of the cooldown. The surrounding after-effects of applying Aspect of Harmony HoTs on your group during the ]vitality withdraw window of Aspect of Harmony simply add to its strengths.

TLDR

Strong rotationally, stronger paired with CDs.

Invoke Yu'lon, the Jade Serpent

One of the two August Celestials of Pandaria we can call to our aid in combat, Invoke Yu'lon, the Jade Serpent, provides passive healing on her own while reducing the mana cost of Enveloping Mist significantly during her active window. This cooldown demands constant activity to maximize its value - Yu'lon rewards players who actively cast throughout her duration.

The Yu'lon Gameplay

During her window, you should cast multiple Enveloping Mists in sequence on different players to:

Generate multiple Renewing Mist buffs via Rapid Diffusion
Set up massive Invigorating Mists healing by following with Vivify casts
Heal those affected by Enveloping Mist!

With , when you first invoke her, your first Tiger Palm or Vivify cast will trigger Courage of the White Tiger, which in turn activates Strength of the Black Ox.

Every Enveloping Mist you cast generates a Renewing Mist that reduces Rising Sun Kick's cooldown through Pool of Mists. While this accelerated pace can feel overwhelming at first, stick to your spell priority and cast abilities as you normally would—the speed will become natural with practice.

Talent Modifiers

Several talents directly enhance Yu'lon's power:

Celestial Harmony applies Chi Cocoon to 5 allies instantly when Yu'lon is invoked, granting small absorb shields. Additionally, this talent increases your Enveloping Mist cast speed by 30% while Yu'lon is active.
You must choose between two playstyle-defining talents:

Gift of the Celestials - Reduces the cooldown from 2 minutes to 1 minute, but halves the duration. This creates more frequent burst windows with shorter uptime.
Jade Bond - Maintains the 2-minute cooldown while significantly amplifying Yu'lon's power:

When Celestial Harmony's Chi Cocoons break, they apply a fresh 4-second Enveloping Mist to each target
Yu'lon's passive Soothing Breath healing is increased by 500%

Yu'lon Cast Sequence Timeline

Important: You can now switch targets freely during your Soothing Mist channel, and the channeled beam will automatically follow your new target. For maximum efficiency, cast Soothing Mist before using several consecutive Enveloping Mist and Vivify to take advantage of the reduced global cooldown. When doing this, ensure you're casting Enveloping Mist on different targets that are currently taking damage or will be taking damage soon, similar to casting Vivify on the most-injured targets within your group.

TLDR

High-activity cooldown that rewards constant casting with massive throughput.

Invoke Chi-Ji, the Red Crane

One of the two August Celestials of Pandaria we can call to our aid in combat, Invoke Chi-Ji, the Red Crane, delivers most of his healing through Gust of Mists casts. These healing events trigger whenever you use Blackout Kick, Rising Sun Kick, or Spinning Crane Kick, converting your damage into group healing.

The Chi-Ji Gameplay

During his window, Chi-Ji provides healing through two distinct mechanics:
Granting instant-cast Enveloping Mist with reduced mana cost
Healing your allies with Gust of Mists as you press melee abilities

This dual approach creates an incredibly active gameplay loop. Your melee abilities become far more powerful than their standard Ancient Teachings damage-to-healing conversions, while simultaneously allowing you to spot-heal injured targets with instant Enveloping Mist casts. These heal-over-time effects not only deliver strong immediate value but also amplify all subsequent healing dealt to those targets through the heal-amp effect.

While Chi-Ji is active and you're talented into the Hero Talent Tree, your first Tiger Palm or Vivify cast will trigger Courage of the White Tiger, which activates Strength of the Black Ox. Consume this buff immediately for a substantial healing boost.

Understanding Gust of Mists

Chi-Ji's Gust of Mists healing may seem straightforward, but understanding the mechanics allows you to maximize your output. Each melee ability triggers Chi-Ji to heal two different targets with three instances of Gust of Mists, generating six total healing events per trigger.

Rising Sun Kick and Spinning Crane Kick always generate exactly six healing instances, regardless of any modifiers. However, Blackout Kick scales with your Teachings of the Monastery stacks: each additional Blackout Kick from Teachings of the Monastery adds six more healing events, up to a maximum of 30 gusts at 4 stacks.

Vice versa, the more rot-based the damage is, the fewer stacks are required to gain consistent healing throughput.

Talent Modifiers

Several talents directly enhance Chi-Ji's power:
Celestial Harmony applies Chi Cocoon to 5 allies instantly when Chi-Ji is invoked, granting small absorb shields. Additionally, Chi-Ji grants you four Teachings of the Monastery stacks immediately upon invocation, eliminating your ramp-up requirement and letting you dive straight into high-output healing.
You must choose between two playstyle-defining talents:

Gift of the Celestials - Reduces the cooldown from 2 minutes to 1 minute, but halves the duration. This creates more frequent damage-to-healing windows with aggressive, burst-focused gameplay.
Jade Bond - Maintains the 2-minute cooldown while significantly amplifying Chi-Ji's power:

When Celestial Harmony's Chi Cocoons break, they apply a fresh 4-second Enveloping Mist to each target
Chi-Ji's Gust of Mists healing is increased by 20%

TLDR

Damage-focused cooldown that converts combat actions into massive passive healing.

Revival

An iconic spell in Mistweaver's spellbook - Revival. This long-cooldown ability delivers all of its healing upfront in a single global cooldown, hitting every single member of your group the moment you activate it. This makes Revival one of the most powerful panic heals in the game, capable of instantly stabilizing your entire raid during critical moments.

Healing and Dispelling

Beyond its raw healing power, Revival carries an additional benefit: it dispels Poison, Disease, and Magic-based effects from every ally it touches. Due to PvP balancing, Revival can only remove up to 3 effects from a single target, but it will dispel every single ally that the spell reaches. This makes it exceptionally powerful for encounters that apply multiple painful debuffs requiring immediate removal across the entire raid.

Functionally, Mistweavers will tend to want to pair the cooldown with a moment of dispelling, but it is important to note that Revival functionally heals first then dispels, not allowing for those pesky bomb-like dispels that deal damage across the entire raid to be dispelled then healed.

 Restoral - The Safer Alternative

We have the option of talenting into Revival's counterpart, Restoral, which trades away the ability to dispel Magic-based effects in exchange for more controlled usage. This choice is typically made in Raid encounters where mass-dispelling magical effects could trigger catastrophic consequences.

For example, during the Anub'arash encounter on Mythic difficulty, dispelling Stinging Swarm from the entire raid simultaneously can cause a raid wipe. In these scenarios, Restoral allows healers to handle dispels individually while preserving the emergency healing component of the cooldown for any critical moment. An added bonus: Restoral can be cast while stunned, though this has limited PvE applications.

Talent Modifiers

Mistweaver has a single talent that enhances Revival: Uplifted Spirits. This talent reduces the cooldown from 3 minutes to 2 minutes 30 seconds while also increasing Revival's healing output by 15%. The shorter cooldown allows for more frequent emergency uses throughout an encounter, making it valuable in fights with multiple dangerous damage spikes.

TLDR

Instant raid-wide heal with mass dispel utility.

Life Cocoon

Mistweaver's external comes in the form of Life Cocoon, which visually wraps an ally in a bright green bubble and lifts them off the ground, ensuring their safety for a limited duration. This ability applies a large absorb shield to its target, protecting them from all forms of damage while they're encased in the cocoon.

Strength of the External

While it's not damage reduction in the traditional sense, Life Cocoon is an incredibly powerful external tool for both DPS and healers. It excels in both proactive and reactive situations, but understanding how absorbs work compared to damage reduction is key to maximizing its value.

Consider this example: A player is sitting at 10,000 health (10% of their max health). If they receive a damage reduction external like Pain Suppression, their effective health pool increases by 40% to 14,000 damage before death. Now let's say we, the Mistweaver about to cast Life Cocoon, have 100,000 health. Our Life Cocoon would provide an absorb shield worth 48,000 points of damage, bringing that player's effective health pool to 58,000 points of damage before death.

The lower your target's health, the more valuable Life Cocoon becomes at preventing their death. That said, even on healthy targets, a 48,000-point absorb shield remains incredibly valuable when players lack their own damage reduction cooldowns or when heavy incoming damage is expected.

Life Cocoon also shines in soak mechanics—Mistweavers can often use their external to solo soak mechanics that would normally require multiple players or defensive cooldowns.

Talent Modifiers

Your talent tree offers several powerful modifiers to enhance Life Cocoon:

TLDR

Massive absorb that scales better the lower your target's health.

Sheilun's Gift

A once iconic artifact trait from the mighty Sheilun, Staff of the Mists, wielded by Emperor Shaohao, lends us his power in the form of Sheilun's Gift - an AoE group-heal that generates clouds around the Mistweaver during combat. Each cloud amplifies the healing power of your next cast, stacking up to create massive burst healing potential.

How It Works

In this iteration, Sheilun's Gift functions as a replacement for Vivify, inheriting nearly all of Vivify's modifying talents while adding its own unique benefits. Clouds generate passively every 8 seconds while in combat and persist until you leave combat for 60 seconds, allowing you to build and maintain stacks between pulls.

Any talent that mentions Vivify will also apply to Sheilun's Gift, with one critical exception: Invigorating Mists. With Invigorating Mists, Vivify, and Sheilun's Gift operate as separate spells. Vivify triggers the standard effect (healing all allies with Renewing Mist), while Sheilun's Gift receives a massive 500% healing increase on its primary target only. This makes target selection crucial - always cast Sheilun's Gift on your most injured ally to maximize the benefit of this interaction.

Even at 0 stacks, Sheilun's Gift functions as a stronger version of Vivify by cleaving healing onto multiple targets. As clouds accumulate, the spell transforms into one of the most powerful spot-heal tools in your arsenal.

Timing and Usage

Understanding when to spam Sheilun's Gift versus holding it for incoming damage is key to mastering the ability. You can strategically time your cast to land right as AoE damage hits your group, delivering a massive emergency heal. Balance cloud generation with tactical usage - sometimes saving stacks for a critical moment is more valuable than spending them immediately.

Talent Modifiers

Core Modifiers (Nearly Mandatory):
Veil of Pride - Doubles cloud generation speed from every 8 seconds to every 4 seconds, dramatically accelerating your ramp-up.
Tranquil Tea - Transforms Mana Tea into a cloud-generation tool, granting 1 cloud per stack of Mana Tea consumed.

Playstyle Modifiers (Situational):
Legacy of Wisdom - Converts Sheilun's Gift from a 3-target heal (1 primary + 2 random allies) to a guaranteed 5-target heal, while reducing the cast time by 0.5 seconds. Exceptional for 5-man content, where you'll hit the entire group every cast.
Emperor's Favor - Shifts from AoE to single-target focus, increasing healing on the primary target by 20% and making every cast instant. Perfect for spot-healing priority targets.

TLDR

Vivify replacement that builds stacks for massive burst healing.

Celestial Conduit

Celestial Conduit, given to us if we decide to be a , delivers substantial healing to allies and damage to enemies over a short channeled duration, and should be used as frequently as your group requires. This is the gateway to Unity Within, the capstone talent Hero Tree, which summons all four August Celestials alongside empowered versions of their associated talents. The cooldown's power is split roughly 50/50 between the channeled healing and the celestial summon effects.

Summoning the Celestials

While channeling Celestial Conduit, you can press the ability again to summon the August Celestials early—though they'll also arrive automatically when the channel completes (or, if interrupted, where the channel would have completed). This flexibility allows you to decide when their effects trigger:
Courage of the White Tiger and Flight of the Red Crane deliver immediate burst healing
Note that Flight of the Red Crane no longer exists as a standalone effect and only occurs with Unity Within.

Strength of the Black Ox applies absorb shields to multiple allies
Heart of the Jade Serpent accelerates the cooldown of affected spells

The key decision point: if you've positioned yourself to avoid losing casts due to Yu'lon's cooldown acceleration, you can summon the Celestials early to access their effects sooner. Otherwise, let the channel complete naturally to maximize the value of each cast.

Managing Yu'lon's "Haste"

While most Celestial effects are automatic, Heart of the Jade Serpent requires active management. For 8 seconds, Yu'lon reduces the cooldown time of Renewing Mist, Rising Sun Kick, Thunder Focus Tea, and Life Cocoon by 150%—effectively making them come off cooldown 2.5x faster.

With Pool of Mists talented, the rapid-fire cooldown reduction on Renewing Mist and Rising Sun Kick can feel overwhelming at first. The rotation speeds up dramatically, with abilities becoming available much faster than you're accustomed to. Success will come from acclimating to the accelerated pace and reacting quickly to those abilities as they come off cooldown.

TLDR

Strong healing channel that summons all four Celestials with empowered effects.

 Mistweaver Monk Advanced Tips

 Renewing Mist Jumps

Renewing Mist is an interesting ability that we use constantly in all forms of content, but it has some unique pieces of functionality worth highlighting to ensure you're getting the most out of it. The multiple-charged spell has a clever component: if the HoT effect heals a target past their maximum health (overhealing), it will attempt to jump to another random eligible target. An eligible target is one that is:
Within 20 yards of the player who has the Renewing Mist
Does not already have a Renewing Mist
Is injured

A jump will also be triggered if you cast a fresh Renewing Mist on a target that already has one, as the older Renewing Mist gets replaced and jumps away but again, only if there is an eligible target. This portion of the spell's functionality makes it incredibly good for spreading healing across your group, as it will (almost) always be on a target that is injured, causing little overhealing unless there are no eligible targets for it to jump to.

"Can I press Renewing Mist on myself and have it auto-target?" is a question that comes up often, but the answer is "not necessarily." If you cast Renewing Mist on yourself (or another target consistently) and then cast another one, the old one will attempt to jump to another target. If an eligible target exists, it will jump to them. If there is no eligible target (meaning no injured allies within 20 yards who don't already have a Renewing Mist), the old one will simply pandemic on yourself, adding duration up to +30% of its original value. In that case, you've effectively lost a Renewing Mist for your group since no eligible targets were in range, even if there were injured allies just outside that 20-yard window.

Thanks to Dancing Mists, we can use this mechanic to our advantage by intentionally targeting someone who already has Renewing Mist to force a jump, giving it a chance to immediately split via the talent. That said, it's a high-risk, high-reward play since if there are no eligible targets within 20 yards, the Renewing Mist will simply refresh on the same target rather than splitting, making a big loss for your overall healing.

Dancing Mists, though, naturally does this during high intensity healing where health bars are jumping to 100% and back down rapidly, as Renewing Mists are flying between targets at an incredible pace.

 Soothing Mist

 Soothing Mist is a channeled, 8-second long healing over time spell that grants you the ability to instantly cast Vivify, Sheilun's Gift, and Enveloping Mist during its channeled duration. Unique to Soothing Mist, the mana cost of the spell is built into the channel its self, meaning that you are paying the mana-tax for every tick of the spell rather than entirely upfront. Let's break Soothing Mist down into several of its key components.

 Global Cooldown

 The global cooldown is a 1.5-second cooldown (lowered by haste) that is triggered after every spell cast across the entire game. Soothing Mist has a special exception to this rule: its activation only triggers a 1-second global cooldown. This is important to keep in mind as we discuss the later sections, since this can potentially save us time (or cost us time) when we utilize the instant casts granted by Soothing Mist.

 Instant Casts

 A major boon to Soothing Mist is the ability to instantly cast Vivify, Sheilun's Gift, and Enveloping Mist during its channel. Each ability triggers the 1.5-second global cooldown as normal, but happen at the beginning of the global cooldown (immediately) rather than at the end of their respective casts (if used without Soothing Mist).

 Enveloping Mist

 In Enveloping Mist's case, we take the 2-second base cast time and reduce it to an instant, invoking the 1.5-second global cooldown instead. This saves 0.5 seconds per cast, however we have to account for the 1-second global cooldown from Soothing Mist's activation. If casting only a single Enveloping Mist, the time savings are completely negated by the Soothing Mist global cooldown, resulting in a 0.5-second time loss rather than a gain.

 You could argue that the faster application of Enveloping Mist combined with the extra HoT ticking from Soothing Mist is worth the time loss, but the counterpoint is that we could have been pressing other abilities more quickly that might do more healing overall.

 As shown below, the time savings from Soothing Mist only kick in after the second Enveloping Mist cast. Avoid using Soothing Mist before Enveloping Mist casts unless you are certain you will be casting several abilities afterward for emergency healing or ramping multiple Enveloping Mists.

 Vivify and Sheilun's Gift

 For Vivify (and by extension Sheilun's Gift with Legacy of Wisdom talented, which we would have at all times), the base cast time is already 1.5 seconds, the same as the global cooldown. This means there is no time saving when casting either of these spells inside Soothing Mist, though you do receive the healing slightly faster as a result. You should never use Soothing Mist before a single cast of Vivify or Sheilun's Gift, as there is no time saving to be had.

 As shown in the graph, we will consistently be 1 second behind if we choose to open with Soothing Mist before several casts.

 Both

 Considering that healing is returned faster for both spell casts, when you need emergency healing on a target that requires several casts back to back, Soothing Mist is your best option, albeit at a slight 0.5-second time loss overall since we gained 0.5 seconds on the instant Enveloping Mist cast.

 Jade Serpent Statue

 Summon Jade Serpent Statue is a Class Tree talent that can be used in conjunction with Soothing Mist for additional healing via the statue's passive. When the statue is active and you begin channeling Soothing Mist, the statue will begin channeling its own Soothing Mist on the same target, effectively increasing the total Soothing Mist healing by 1.5x for the duration. Even if your channel ends early, the statue will continue its own Soothing Mist channel for the full 8-second duration.

 Teachings of the Monastery

 Mistweaver has a baseline mechanic that drives a few of our spec's interactions in Teachings of the Monastery. This passive grants us a stack of the self-named buff for every Tiger Palm that strikes an enemy, up to a maximum of 4 stacks. With each stack, an additional Blackout Kick hits the enemy with each having an individual chance of 20% to reset the remaining cooldown on Rising Sun Kick. This gives us some room to play with probability and chance to aim for resets on one of our core abilities throughout the kit.

 With Way of the Crane, aim for 2 stacks before pressing Blackout Kick. With Way of the Serpent, press Blackout Kick at 0 stacks. The math behind these different strategies reveals why GCD efficiency matters more than raw reset chance.

 Rising Sun Kick Reset Probability

 More Blackout Kick hits means better odds at a reset. Each hit independently rolls a 20% chance to reset Rising Sun Kick, so the probability of getting at least one reset scales with your Teachings of the Monastery stacks:
 Reset chance = 1 - (0.8) ^ (1 + stacks)
 

 Teachings of the Monastery Stacks Blackout Kick Hits Reset Chance 
 0 1 20.00% 
 1 2 36.00% 
 2 3 48.80% 
 3 4 59.04% 
 4 5 67.23% 
 

 While more stacks always mean a higher absolute reset chance, the real question isn't "how likely is a reset?" but rather "how many GCDs did I spend building those stacks?" This is where Way of the Crane and Way of the Serpent diverge sharply in their approach to resets.

 Way of the Crane

 With Way of the Crane, each Tiger Palm strikes the enemy twice, granting 2 Teachings of the Monastery stacks per cast. This means you reach meaningful stack counts in fewer GCDs, changing the optimal strategy for resets entirely.

 

 Teachings of the Monastery Stacks Tiger Palm GCDs Total GCDs Reset Chance Resets per GCD 
 0 0 1 20.00% 0.200 
 2 1 2 48.80% 0.244 
 4 2 3 67.23% 0.224 
 

 The sweet spot for Way of the Crane is 2 stacks - one Tiger Palm into Blackout Kick. Despite having a lower absolute reset chance than 4 stacks, the single GCD investment yields the highest resets per GCD at 0.244. Going to 4 stacks costs an extra GCD for only ~18% more reset chance, dropping your efficiency back down below where you started at 0 stacks.

 Way of the Serpent

 With Way of the Serpent, each Tiger Palm strikes only once, granting 1 Teachings of the Monastery stack per cast. Every additional stack costs a full GCD, and the diminishing returns on reset probability become harsh quickly.

 

 Teachings of the Monastery Stacks Tiger Palm GCDs Total GCDs Reset Chance Resets per GCD 
 0 0 1 20.00% 0.200 
 1 1 2 36.00% 0.180 
 2 2 3 48.80% 0.163 
 3 3 4 59.04% 0.148 
 4 4 5 67.23% 0.134 
 

 For Way of the Serpent, just press Blackout Kick immediately at 0 stacks. Every Tiger Palm you cast before Blackout Kick costs a full GCD, but the marginal reset probability per GCD only shrinks. You're better off fishing for the 20% reset as often as possible rather than investing GCDs into building stacks that yield diminishing returns. Only use Tiger Palm as filler when Blackout Kick's 2-second cooldown is active.

 Cooldown Awareness

 Regardless of your stance, always check Rising Sun Kick's remaining cooldown before pressing Blackout Kick. If Rising Sun Kick has ~3 seconds or less remaining, press Rising Sun Kick first, then Blackout Kick immediately after. A reset is wasted if it overwrites a nearly-finished cooldown (let alone a fully-finished cooldown). Use filler abilities to wait out the last few seconds if needed, then Rising Sun Kick into Blackout Kick for a meaningful reset chance.

 Thunder Focus Tea "Combos"

 While we often in Raid choose the best overall option, there are some fun interactions with Thunder Focus Tea that we may execute and/or keep in mind while using it:

 Instant Renewing Mist Extension

 Focused Thunder

 Rising Sun Kick Resets

 Focused Thunder
 Way of the Crane

 These Tiger Palm globals can realistically be filled with any spell of your choice, but gaining Teachings of the Monastery stacks to attempt a reset of Rising Sun Kick (which is the goal of consuming Thunder Focus Tea with Rising Sun Kick in the first place) is an incredibly efficient way to do so. Do note, this realistically cannot happen with since we gain Haste from Flowing Wisdom and Heart of the Jade Serpent grants us increased cooldown speed, effectively removing the in-between ability presses.

 Soothing Mist Spot Healing

 Without Emperor's Elixir, the Thunder Focus Tea isn't strictly required since Soothing Mist already makes Enveloping Mist instant cast, however it still offers value by delivering Enveloping Mist's immediate heal instantly.

 Mists of Life Interaction

 Mists of Life offers an interesting interaction, being that the Renewing Mist that gets applied can also be used as an off-GCD way to consume your Thunder Focus Tea!
